## What is GitHub

- A website for hosting code and tracking versions over time
- Built on Git - version tracking for your files
- Lets you publish web apps for free, with no traditional server
- Used for collaboration, portfolios, and class projects
- [github.com](https://github.com/)

## Repositories and Collaborators

- A Repository is a project folder stored on GitHub, with full history
- Each repository has an owner - a user or organization account
- Collaborators are other GitHub users invited to work on the repository
- Collaborators can edit code, fix bugs, and add features together
- Example: [FIT Retail Index (non-AI)](https://calvinw.github.io/BusMgmtBenchmarks/)

## Public Repositories and Private Repositories

- Public Repositories - anyone on the internet can see the code
  - Good for open source, portfolios, and free web hosting
  - Example: class demos and published apps
- Private Repositories - only you and your collaborators can see it
  - Good for homework, drafts, and work in progress
  - You control who is invited as a collaborator

## Open Source Example: BusMgmtBenchmarks

- [calvinw/BusMgmtBenchmarks](https://github.com/calvinw/BusMgmtBenchmarks) - a public, open source repo
- MIT License - anyone can use, copy, and build on the code
- README describes the project, data, and live web app
- 247 commits show the full history of changes over time
- Live site published for free: [FIT Retail Index](https://calvinw.github.io/BusMgmtBenchmarks/)

## Version Control

- Version control tracks every change to your files over time
- Each saved checkpoint is called a commit, with a message describing it
- You can see history, compare versions, and undo mistakes
- Multiple people can work on the same files without losing work

## Branches on GitHub

- A branch is a separate copy of your code for working on something new
- The main branch is the official, working version of the project
- Create a branch to fix a bug or try a feature without breaking main
- When done, merge the branch back into main

## GitHub Pages

- GitHub Pages publishes your repository as a free website
- No traditional server needed - just HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files
- Repo: [calvinw/BusMgmtBenchmarks](https://github.com/calvinw/BusMgmtBenchmarks)
- Live Pages site: [FIT Retail Index](https://calvinw.github.io/BusMgmtBenchmarks/)
- Address is username.github.io/repository-name
